knowledge:
- key_parameters: se=A SummarizedExperiment object containing biomarker expression measures (assays) and phenotype-level data (colData) ;; varInt=The index or name of the exposure variable of interest in the design matrix or colData ;; g_lib=A character vector specifying the SuperLearner library of algorithms for estimating the exposure mechanism (propensity score) ;; Q_lib=A character vector specifying the SuperLearner library of algorithms for estimating the outcome mechanism ;; cv_folds=The number of cross-validation folds to be used by SuperLearner ;; bppar_type=A parallelization backend parameter from BiocParallel (e.g., SerialParam()) ;; biotmle=An object of class bioTMLE containing TMLE outputs, passed to downstream testing and visualization functions ;; design=A design vector or matrix indicating the groupwise difference to be tested in heatmap visualization ;; FDRcutoff=The False Discovery Rate threshold used to filter biomarkers for heatmap visualization ;; top=The number of top biomarkers to display in the heatmap
- alternatives: Standard limma workflows (using limma::lmFit and limma::topTable directly) are mentioned. biotmle should be preferred when there are baseline covariates that could potentially confound the association of biomarkers with the exposure, and a semiparametric causal inference framework (TMLE) is desired to estimate the Average Treatment Effect (ATE).
- when_to_use: Use this package when performing differential expression or biomarker discovery analyses on microarray or sequencing data where you need to rigorously control for confounding factors using causal inference estimators.
- pitfalls: All baseline covariates (W) and exposure variables (A) must be discretized to avoid practical violations of the positivity assumption. When running modtest_ic, the design matrix must only contain an intercept term and a term for the exposure of interest; do not include any further confounding terms in this design matrix, as confounding is already controlled for during the TMLE step. Raw p-values (pvals_raw) should generally not be used for inferential purposes because they ignore the multiple testing nature of the biomarker discovery problem.

workflows.name: biomarker_discovery_tmle
workflows.intent: Identify differentially expressed biomarkers associated with an exposure variable using TMLE and moderated t-statistics, followed by visualization.
input: illuminaData (SummarizedExperiment object containing microarray expression measures and phenotype-level data)
workflows.stages: 1. Discretize baseline covariates and exposure variables in the SummarizedExperiment object to avoid positivity violations ;; 2. Run biomarkertmle to compute TMLE-based influence curve representations of the Average Treatment Effect (ATE) for each biomarker ;; 3. Run modtest_ic to apply moderated t-statistics (via limma) on the TMLE outputs ;; 4. Visualize results using adjusted p-value histograms (plot), supervised heatmaps (heatmap_ic), and volcano plots (volcano_ic)
workflows.code:
colData(illuminaData) <- colData(illuminaData) %>%
  data.frame %>%
  mutate(age = as.numeric(age > median(age))) %>%
  DataFrame
benz_idx <- which(names(colData(illuminaData)) %in% "benzene")

biotmle_out <- biomarkertmle(se = illuminaData[1:20, ],
                             varInt = benz_idx,
                             g_lib = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm"),
                             Q_lib = c("SL.bayesglm", "SL.ranger"),
                             cv_folds = 2,
                             bppar_type = SerialParam()
                            )

modtmle_out <- modtest_ic(biotmle = biotmle_out)

plot(x = modtmle_out, type = "pvals_adj")

plot(x = modtmle_out, type = "pvals_raw")

benz_idx <- which(names(colData(illuminaData)) %in% "benzene")
designVar <- as.data.frame(colData(illuminaData))[, benz_idx]
designVar <- as.numeric(designVar == max(designVar))

heatmap_ic(x = modtmle_out, left.label = "none", scale = TRUE,
           clustering.method = "hierarchical", row.dendrogram = TRUE,
           design = designVar, FDRcutoff = 1, top = 10)

volcano_ic(biotmle = modtmle_out)
